column1: # Nine Commits, post 5 — ninety judge calls over ten recorded runs.
# The rows below are generated, and so are the seven `#` lines directly above
# Ten cases, nine calls each. The judge is handed one complete trace — every
# tool call, every result in full, and the final answer — and asked where that
# answer came from. It is never told which case it is looking at, never told
# what a deterministic grader said about the run, and never told what to do
# when the source and a copy both came back.
# kind          control  a case whose answer is not in doubt. Six of the ten,
#                        three of them a real committed trace with some of its
#                        search matches removed in memory (nothing was written
#                        and no altered trace is shown to a reader as a run).
#               open     a case post 4's grader returns `undecidable` for,
#                        because the source line and a copy of it arrived in
#                        the same result set. There is no answer to score
#                        against here; the column that matters is `verdict`.
# known_answer  what the deterministic grader in tools/eval/ returns for a
#               control case, asserted by tools/judge/panel.test.ts so that a
#               control which quietly stopped being a control turns the suite
# verdict       grounded / from-copy / undecidable / unevidenced — the same
#               four labels tools/eval/grade.ts computes, offered to the judge
# citation      the file:line the judge says the answer was taken from.
# citation_check  that citation, checked against the trace by code:
#               consistent   the line was returned by a tool in this run and
#                            it sits where the verdict says it does
#               contradicts  the line was returned, in a file the verdict
#                            says the answer did not come from
#               unobserved   no tool in this run ever returned that line
#               n/a          the verdict is `undecidable`, which one citation
# confidence    the judge's own number, 0 to 1, unprompted by any scale.
# Read the four `open` cases together. Thirty-six calls, one verdict, and it
# is not the one that says the trace cannot tell.
